title: The Effect of Static and Dynamic Stretching during Warm-Up on Running Economy and Perception of Effort in Recreational Endurance Runners
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (MDPI)
claims: The studied warm-up combined 10 minutes of running with 5 minutes of static or dynamic stretching; the no-stretching session consisted of 15 minutes of running.
Both static and dynamic stretching within the warm-up improved running economy and lowered perceived exertion compared with running only, in recreational endurance runners.
Stretching duration matters: medium stretch durations (at most about 90 s) were associated with improved running economy, while long durations (at least 120 s) showed no beneficial effect.
